reasoning_summary: Step-by-step check of the reduction Hamiltonian Path <=p LongPath17. Lines 0004-0005 (membership in NP) and 0006-0010 (Hamiltonian Path is NP-complete) are standard. Lines 0011-0018: G = H plus 17 isolated vertices; construction is poly-time (O(1) extra vertices) and |VG| = n+17, so the target path length |VG|-17 equals n. Forward direction (0020-0028): a Hamiltonian path of H is literally a path in G using only edges of EH subset EG, visiting exactly n = |VG|-17 vertices; justified. Backward direction (0029-0049): PG visits exactly n vertices; the load-bearing justification is at 0034-0042 -- no isolated u_i can lie on a path with more than one vertex since it has no incident edges, so PG lies entirely inside the H-component and, having n = |VH| distinct vertices, is exactly a Hamiltonian path of H (edges of EG between VH-vertices are exactly EH, line 0047-0048). The biconditional therefore holds and the reduction is correct. Two blemishes, neither fatal: (i) line 0033-0034 asserts 'any set of n distinct vertices of G must include all the original vertices VH (and possibly some of the added ones)', which is false as stated (n=3 with VH={v1,v2,v3} and U-vertices: {v1,u1,u2} is a set of 3 distinct vertices of G missing v2,v3) and is internally inconsistent with its own parenthetical; however the proof does not use this claim -- the correct conclusion PG subset VH is obtained independently from the isolated-vertex/component argument that immediately follows, so the derivation is unaffected. (ii) Line 0040 writes 'since PG visits n > 1 vertices', tacitly assuming n > 1; for the degenerate instance n = 1 a one-vertex path at some u_i does witness |VG|-17 = 1, but H (a single vertex) does have a Hamiltonian path, so the equivalence still holds and the reduction remains correct for every instance. Since Hamiltonian Path is NP-hard and the map is poly-time computable with a valid yes/no correspondence, the NP-hardness conclusion (0050-0054) follows.
